title: Eight years
logline: Eight. The corn. Two days before twenty-five. The strip keeps them separate on purpose.

panels.composition: The garage. A tray of corn on the drafting table. WOOD. BARNABY. The chorus, small at the back, holding a sign: AGAIN?

image.prompt: a man at a drafting table with a paper tray of corn, a dog, and small stick figures at the back of the panel holding a sign reading AGAIN?, muddy flats

balloons.text: Every year. It's the twelfth. It's corn. Thursday is my birthday and that's cake and that's separate.

image.prompt: a man explaining something to stick figures with tired patience

panels.composition: #1 on the wall. The cafeteria. Wood's eyes on it. Eight years of ink between then and the corn.

image.prompt: close-up of a yellowed old comic strip pinned to a garage wall, a man's reflection faint in its plastic sleeve

panels.composition: Alone at the long surface. The corn. The dog. The chorus has, for once, nothing to say.

image.prompt: a man at a long drafting table with his back turned, a tray of corn, a dog, stick figures at the back of the panel saying nothing, no words
